strategies.title: [ruin-recreate-neighborhood] Critical-model destroy-and-regret-rebuild

strategies.title: [tabu-bottleneck-relocation] Tabu-guided bottleneck relocation with aspiration
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: tabu-bottleneck-relocation  
Replacement scope: Replace the final one-pass “Repartition the current worst GPU with each partner” block after the MILP phase.  
Compute budget: At most 80 accepted or evaluated tabu iterations per call; each iteration evaluates only moves of models from the two highest-pressure GPUs to all feasible destination GPUs, plus swaps between those two source GPUs and all other GPUs. Expected evaluation-time effect: small bounded increase, generally below the existing large pair-enumeration cost.  
Gain mechanism: The incumbent only permits one exact two-GPU repartition involving the initially worst GPU, so it cannot intentionally accept a neutral or slightly adverse intermediate relocation that frees capacity for a later bottleneck-reducing relocation. strategies.title: [pressure-window-set-partition] Critical-window exact subsystem replacement
strategies.plan:

Compute budget: At most 3 subsystem windows per call; each window contains the 3 highest-pressure GPUs and all models currently assigned to them, capped at 22 models by retaining the highest `load + incumbent_max_pressure * size` models and treating remaining models as fixed background. Gain mechanism: Instead of changing the partition of only two GPUs, solve the coupled repartition of a three-GPU pressure window. Maintain incremental `(used_size, load)` state; prune a branch if any GPU has nonpositive free memory or its current pressure already exceeds the best full-placement maximum. Seed the search with the current assignment and explore model order descending by `load + T*size`, where `T` is the current maximum KVPR. Fixed background models remain on their original GPU, so the subsystem always has a valid incumbent. Accept a replacement only after exact recomputation confirms every GPU fits and the global maximum KVPR strictly decreases.  
Expected-gain check: this adds three-way redistribution of a critical model, its capacity donor, and its load recipient—a feasible contact topology unavailable to the incumbent’s two-bin split—and is falsified unless evaluation exceeds `combined_score 26.2559717495`.

strategies.title: [lagrangian-price-construction] Dual-price structural reconstruction
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: lagrangian-price-construction  
Replacement scope: Replace the initial single descending-load greedy construction, while keeping the subsequent MILP and final exact polishing phases unchanged.  
Compute budget: Exactly 6 deterministic construction starts and at most 12 price-update rounds per start; no additional external optimizer. Expected evaluation-time effect: modest linear-time overhead in `models × GPUs × 72`, normally much smaller than the existing MILP calls.  
Gain mechanism: Construct placements under dynamically updated GPU scarcity prices rather than using only the current ratio. For each start use one of six fixed model orders: descending load, size, `load/size`, `load + lower_bound*size`, and the reverse tie-break variants of the first two. In each price-update round, rebuild from scratch: assign each model to a feasible GPU minimizing its resulting maximum KVPR plus a GPU-specific price times resulting consumed memory, with deterministic tie-breaking. Update each GPU’s price by projected ascent from its excess over the current average transformed demand `load + T*size`, where `T` is the best current construction pressure; normalize prices to zero mean. Keep the best exact feasible construction as the MILP incumbent. This changes the initial assignment basin presented to the time-limited MILP and pair optimizer, especially when the MILP has no proven solution before its deadline. Capacity is protected by rejecting choices with residual memory at most `eps`; if a reconstruction cannot place every model, discard it.  
Expected-gain check: the incumbent has only one unpriced greedy basin whereas this construction explicitly prices future scarcity before MILP rounding; it is accepted only if the evaluator’s measured `combined_score` is strictly above `26.2559717495`.

strategies.title: [global-bmatching-repair] Threshold-slack simultaneous relocation repair
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: global-bmatching-repair

Replacement scope: Replace the post-MILP “repartition the current worst GPU with each partner” block with a bounded global threshold-repair phase operating on all GPUs simultaneously.

Compute budget: At most 8 target-pressure repair rounds; each round considers at most the 24 highest-pressure source models and builds one deterministic augmenting bipartite assignment. No external optimizer starts; expected evaluation-time effect is small, approximately \(O(8 \cdot n \cdot gpu\_num)\) candidate checks plus matching.

Gain mechanism: The current polishing only repacks the initially worst GPU with one partner, so it cannot execute a coordinated set of relocations where several destination GPUs each absorb one model and jointly free enough pressure/memory for the bottleneck GPU. For a target \(T\) slightly below the incumbent maximum KVPR, compute each GPU’s transformed slack \(80T-\sum_i(load_i+T size_i)\). Treat models on GPUs exceeding \(T\) as source items, add an edge from item \(i\) to destination GPU \(g\) only when moving it leaves its source and destination with positive residual memory and moves both transformed loads toward feasibility, then find a maximum-cardinality/minimum-pressure-increase matching. Apply the full matching only if the exact recomputed maximum KVPR strictly decreases. Repeat from the new bottleneck; preserve the incumbent if no full repair improves it. Every edge is prevalidated against memory, and the committed matching is revalidated with exact size sums before emission. Expected-gain check: this can realize a simultaneous many-source-to-many-destination relocation topology that the incumbent’s one-worst-GPU/two-bin replacement cannot realize, and it is falsified unless the evaluator reports combined_score strictly above 26.2559717495.

strategies.title: [configuration-master-partitioning] Feasible-bin configuration master problem
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: configuration-master-partitioning

Replacement scope: Replace the binary-search assignment-variable MILP phase, from its SciPy imports through `bins = best`, with a bounded configuration-generation feasibility master.

Compute budget: At most 14 pressure-bound trials; for each trial enumerate at most 30,000 feasible GPU configurations using depth-first subset generation, retain at most 6,000 nondominated configurations, and solve one set-partitioning MILP with a 0.20 second limit. Expected evaluation-time effect is moderate and bounded; skip this phase and retain greedy placement when \(n>24\).

Gain mechanism: At a fixed pressure bound \(T\), a valid GPU contents set must satisfy both `sum(size) < 80` and `sum(load + T*size) <= 80*T`. Generate such whole-bin configurations directly, discard any configuration dominated by another configuration covering a subset of its models with no greater resource use, then solve a master exact-cover problem: each model must occur in exactly one selected configuration and at most `gpu_num` configurations may be selected. Unlike the incumbent assignment MILP, the master chooses complete compatible packs as atomic columns, exposing packing complementarities between a high-size/low-load model and a low-size/high-load model before integer branching. Decode only integral selected columns, verify each model appears once and every residual memory is positive, and retain the prior incumbent on any incomplete generation or failed solve. Expected-gain check: the configuration master can branch on complete feasible packs rather than independent model-GPU variables, a packing degree of freedom absent from the incumbent formulation, and it is falsified unless it produces an evaluator combined_score above 26.2559717495.

strategies.title: [conflict-directed-binpacking] Symmetry-pruned feasibility branch-and-bound
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: conflict-directed-binpacking

Replacement scope: Replace both the greedy construction and the SciPy binary-search MILP phase with a deterministic exact-feasibility branch-and-bound initializer; retain the existing final pair-repartition phase as a cheap finishing step.

Compute budget: At most 16 pressure-bound bisection trials and 120,000 DFS nodes per trial; no optimizer starts. Expected evaluation-time effect is bounded and usually lower than repeated short MILP launches on small and medium instances; immediately fall back to the current greedy construction after a node limit.

Gain mechanism: For a candidate \(T\), branch on the unassigned model with largest transformed weight `load + T*size` (ties by size and load), and place it into feasible bins in increasing resulting transformed load order. Canonicalize identical bin states by only branching once among bins with the same `(used_size, transformed_load)` signature. Prune with: total remaining transformed capacity, total remaining memory, each item’s feasible-bin count, and a conflict test that rejects a node when any pair of unassigned models cannot coexist in any currently possible bin and there are insufficient distinct bins for the resulting conflict clique. A found leaf is an exact feasible assignment for that bound; bisection retains the best verified leaf. This changes the search representation from a generic MILP incumbent search to a bin-packing conflict tree with GPU-symmetry elimination, while every branch enforces strictly positive residual memory. Expected-gain check: conflict pruning and identical-bin symmetry permit exploring complete assignments at pressure bounds that the incumbent’s time-limited assignment MILP may classify as infeasible, and it is falsified unless the evaluator combined_score exceeds 26.2559717495.
